newsitem.title: MEXICO: Moderna Q1 weak but may improve-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Moderna Q1 weak but may improve-analysts.

text.p: First quarter earnings posted by Mexican conglomerate Empresas La Moderna were weak but due to what were hopefully temporary setbacks, analysts said.
La Moderna posted net consolidated earnings of 427.3 million pesos, equivalent to 93 centavos per share, which compared with an average forecast of 59 centavos from analysts surveyed by Reuters.

Analysts noted, however, that La Moderna's bottom line was bolstered by extraordinary revenues from the partial sales of Asgrow Agronomics division to Monsanto Co, and of its packaging division Empaques Ponderosa.

Earnings by La Moderna's tobacco division were hit by cigarette smuggling in Mexico which forced cigarette makers in general to cut prices during the first quarter. Nonetheless, analysts said they had predicted this would happen, and saw the situation improving later in the year.
"The earnings were below expectations overall, but for reasons that are explainable," said Alyce Andrews, an analyst with Merrill Lynch in New York.
"The figures looked weak at first, but that was partly due to timing issues in the seed business, they were not so bad after all," Francisco Chavez of Smith Barney in New York said.
La Moderna incorporated fourth quarter 1996 earnings by its Seminis seed division in its overall earnings for the first quarter.
Andrews said the main surprise in La Moderna's earnings report had been a small net loss of two million pesos by the agribiotechnology division.
"This was due to delayed seed shipments, which will hopefully be credited next quarter," she said.
The analysts added that La Moderna's first quarter earnings report was a minefield of accountancy adjustments that limited the relevance of year-ago comparisons.
"The Mexican practice of restating revenues in line with inflation makes the situation difficult for companies with foreign sales," Chavez said.

Under Mexican accountancy rules, dollar-based sales are converted in pesos and restated in line with domestic inflation, thus making year-ago foreign sales appear higher than they really were, Chavez said.

Thus, net earnings for the first quarter were down to 427.3 million pesos from a restated year-ago figure of 575.6 million pesos. Total sales were similarly down to 2.971 billion pesos from 3.206 billion pesos over the same period.
